title: XAI data centre may have led to Mississippi air pollution spike | New Scientist
description: Elon Musk firm’s Colossus 2 data centre – the largest in the US – has been spewing out nitrogen oxide emissions from trailer-mounted gas turbines, an analysis suggests
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Earliest alligator flourished in the wake of the dinosaur extinction | New Scientist
description: Just a few hundred thousand years after an asteroid wiped out most dinosaurs, large alligators were thriving in North America
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: AI is both the best and worst thing to ever happen to mathematics | New Scientist
description: Mathematicians now have a formidable tool for breaking open challenging problems, but working out how best to use it isn't going to be easy
author: Timothy Revell

title: Natural feedbacks will warm world an extra 20 per cent this century | New Scientist
description: Ecosystems like wetlands emit more carbon as temperatures rise. By 2100, such feedback loops will increase warming by 20 to 30 per cent more than anticipated
author: Alec Luhn

title: We may finally know what kick-starts muscle contractions in childbirth | New Scientist
description: An influx of immune cells into the uterus may be what initiates childbirth. These grab on to muscle cells via tiny tubes and send across mitochondria to provide energy for contractions
author: Alice Klein

title: Gamma ray burst may have been two supernovae in one | New Scientist
description: A group of astronomers proposes that a series of events in a distant galaxy formed both a black hole and a pulsar, but other experts say the conclusion is premature
author: Matt von Hippel
